title: resume-download-hang-notes
content:
Context:
- Intermittent model load failures in staging: large checkpoint ( ~210 GB tar) will start downloading fine but stalls during resume/seek and never completes. Affects resume logic in blobstream -> tar stream -> shard reader path.
- Repro rate ~3/20 downloads in staging (k8s). Prod unaffected so far but worried about edge-case on poor networks.

Symptoms observed (from agent + proxy logs):
- Client issues GET with Range header to GCS signed URL. Typically requests range starting at byte N where N is resume offset.
- Server returns: HTTP/1.1 200 OK (not 206) for range request in ~30% of failing cases -> client code treats as fallback but then confusion in Content-Length vs expected remaining bytes.
- When 200 is returned we see Content-Length ~= full object and streaming attempt does chunked transfer; our BlobStream expects Content-Range/206 and does a single ranged read.
- Often the connection hangs after ~50-200MB transferred; stack shows blocked on read() in python requests (urllib3) with an open socket. Kernel stats show TCP retransmits and then connection reset.

Logs (sanitized):
[2026-02-16T03:14:12Z] blobstream: starting range request url="<signed-url>" range="bytes=137438953472-"
[2026-02-16T03:14:12Z] http-client DEBUG: > GET /... HTTP/1.1
[2026-02-16T03:14:12Z] http-client DEBUG: < HTTP/1.1 200 OK
[2026-02-16T03:14:12Z] http-client DEBUG: < Content-Length: 2251799813685248
[2026-02-16T03:16:03Z] blobstream: read stalled after 123MB transferred; last byte=137562383616
[2026-02-16T03:17:44Z] k8s: pod restart backoff due to readiness probe fail

Reproduction steps I used locally (quick):
1) Create signed URL for object (gsutil signurl)
2) curl with Range header to simulate resume: 
   curl -v -H "Range: bytes=137438953472-" "<signed-url>" -o /tmp/chunk.part
Observations: sometimes curl returns 200 + huge content-length and streams; sometimes returns 206 and only the requested range. The failing case tends to be the 200 response.

Quick experiments (commands tried):
- gsutil -D cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/llama-13b/ckpt-2025-11.tar ./  (works or stalls depending on run)
- curl -v -H "Range: bytes=0-1048575" "<signed-url>"  -> 206 expected, usually OK
- curl -v -H "Range: bytes=137438953472-" "<signed-url>"  -> sometimes 200; when 200: response header Content-Length==object_size (not remaining)
- python requests stream test:
    import requests
    r = requests.get(url, headers={"Range": "bytes=137438953472-"}, stream=True, timeout=(5,120))
    for chunk in r.iter_content(65536):
        process(chunk)
  -> chunk iteration blocks indefinitely after some MB
- tcpdump on node during hang: repeated retransmit (SYN/ACK?) and eventually FIN; remote resets.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Signed URL generation + caching on CDN side: signed URL sometimes routes to a backend that doesn't support range/206 properly (edge case in GCS/Cloud CDN), returning 200 and then inconsistent streaming behaviour.
2) Large resume offset + HTTP/2: interaction between our client (urllib3 over httpx?) and server: http/2 stream flow-control where server advertises large content-length, then stalls if client window not updated.
3) Middleboxes (sidecar/proxy) in k8s (istio/Envoy) rewrites Range headers or mishandles 206 responses for large offsets, causing proxy to buffer and then fail.
4) Tar reader/backpressure bug: our TarStream tries to seek/rewind on a stream that doesn't support random access and we get into a read-then-seek deadlock.

Notes on 206 vs 200 behavior:
- RFC: servers MUST reply 206 for Range if satisfiable. If 200 returned, client must assume server ignored Range. Our code currently treats 200 as 'fallback to full download' but still uses expected remaining bytes to set a read deadline -> mismatch. Need robust handling: if 200, compare Content-Length to expected remaining; if Content-Length > remaining then assume full object and restart with full download or abort.

Data points from telemetry: (last 48h)
- 37 total checkpoints downloaded by staging nodes
- 9 downloads logged partial-range requests (resume)
- 3 downloads stalled for >2 minutes and triggered pod eviction
- Failure cohort: all from nodes in us-central1-c, via node pool with custom sidecar version v1.8.2

Quick patches attempted (on staging):
- Patch blobstream: if response.status_code == 200 and content-length > remaining_bytes: close connection and retry without Range (full download). Reduced hang frequency but increased egress bandwidth (bad).
- Switch http client to requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=100, pool_maxsize=100) to avoid connection reuse oddities; no measurable change.
- Added retry on socket timeout with exponential backoff (max 3). Brought success on 2/3 prior failing runs.

Stack trace (before retry patch) when hung (python):
  File "/app/blobstream.py", line 212, in _stream_range
    for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=65536):
  File "/opt/python/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 753, in iter_content
    for chunk in self.raw.stream(chunk_size, decode_content=True):
  File "/opt/python/lib/python3.10/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 818, in stream
    data = self.read(amt=amt, decode_content=decode_content)
  File "/opt/python/lib/python3.10/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 624, in read
    data = self._fp.read(amt)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/http/client.py", line 458, in read
    s = self.sock.recv(left)
# blocked here until socket closes

Ideas to probe next (short checklist):
- [ ] Collect server-side GCS logs for signed URL accesses around timestamps: 2026-02-16T03:10-03:20Z (ask infra for logs). Need to check if 206 or 200 was returned upstream.
- [ ] Reproduce with direct GCS XML API (no signed URL) to rule out CDN/signed-url layer.
- [ ] Try curl --http1.1 to force HTTP/1.1 vs default http2 to test flow-control hypothesis.
- [ ] Run test with no sidecar (bypass istio) on a few nodes to check proxy influence.
- [ ] Add more aggressive detection in blobstream: if read stalls for >15s and bytes_transferred < min_rate then abort and retry. Record metrics (bytes/sec) for postmortem.
- [ ] Validate tar reader path: make sure we do not attempt to seek on streaming response; convert to read-and-write-to-tempfile when resume not supported.

Notes-to-self:
- Edge case may be combination of server returning 200 + client expecting partial content and then holding on to socket for long time. Fixing to treat 200 as a hard mismatch and immediately restart full download or abort seems the safest short-term fix.
- Long-term: support resumable downloads via GCS compose / chunked upload pattern or use objectRange RPCs that are guaranteed to return 206.

Open questions:
- Why would GCS signed URL sometimes route to a node that returns 200 for a Range request? Is there a backend version skew?
- Are there load-balancers in front of GCS that rewrite Range?
- Is our signed URL malformed when resume offset > 2^32? (unlikely but check)

Useful links / refs:
- GCS signed URL docs (range requests): https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls
- RFC7233 Range Requests: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233
- GitHub issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/612 (related: tar streaming/backpressure)

Next actions (short term):
1) Push blobstream quick fix: detect 200-on-range -> abort and retry without range (or switch to tempfile), add metric -> rollout to staging canary.
2) Run controlled reproduce forcing http1.1 vs http2 and sidecar on/off.
3) File ENGINF follow-up to collect GCS edge logs and ask Cloud support if signed URL behavior is expected.

-- Lucas
